data.body:
CORRECTION + CURRENT-MAIN VERIFICATION (supersedes my prior "ROOT CAUSE" comment's framing)

## Reconciliation with the earlier RebarBotNava comment — it was RIGHT
RebarBotNava's correction comment above is the correct diagnosis, and I am revising my
previous comment to match it. The ACTIVE cause was NOT a standing defect in
`_network_guard`; it was e9d5's own new fixture `effect_spies`
(tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_payload_shadow_effect_spies.py) patching
`socket.socket.connect`/`connect_ex` via **monkeypatch.setattr** while the autouse
`_network_guard` patch was active. monkeypatch restores a class attr by a plain
snapshot setattr/delattr that is NOT aware the attribute was already made local by another
active patch, so its teardown re-`setattr`'d `_network_guard`'s guard back **permanently**
onto the worker — blocking every later `allow_network` test (test_serve) on that worker.
That reproduces deterministically WITHOUT xdist (run that file's tests, then test_serve, in
one worker), so "only under full-suite parallel load" was a red herring.

## This is ALREADY FIXED on origin/main — verified
The fix landed as part of e9d5 in commit **d46c332c6740** ("e9d5: typed mutation payload
union + comparator", 2026-08-30 23:26Z), which is an ancestor of current origin/main
(HEAD 5c28ce66). `effect_spies` now uses `unittest.mock.patch.object` for connect/connect_ex
(LIFO-correct, composes with `_network_guard`), and the file ships a dedicated regression
test `test_effect_spies_do_not_leak_socket_connect_into_later_tests`.

Empirical verification I ran on a fresh worktree at current origin/main (5c28ce66), clean tree:
- Deterministic repro (the RebarBotNava recipe): `pytest <effect_spies file> <test_serve file>
  -p no:randomly` in ONE worker, no xdist → **9 passed, 1 skipped**; test_serve GREEN.
- Broad sequential sweep: entire `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/` dir THEN test_serve,
  one worker → **684 passed, 2 skipped**; test_serve GREEN.
- Named regression test → **1 passed**.
- Invariant probe: nesting two `patch.object(socket.socket,"connect",...)` windows (outer =
  guard, inner = effect_spies' _boom) and tearing down LIFO leaves
  `'connect' in socket.socket.__dict__ == False` → correctly restored to the inherited real,
  NO leak.
- Grep sweep: `effect_spies` is the ONLY guarded-tier (tests/unit, tests/scripts) test that
  patches `socket.socket.connect`/`connect_ex` at all; the other socket monkeypatches in the
  tier touch `socket.getfqdn`/`gethostname`/`socketserver`, which cannot leak the connect
  guard. So there is no remaining live seed.

## Correcting my prior comment
My prior comment framed `_network_guard` as "not restore-safe" and proposed hardening it.
That was over-stated as the ACTIVE cause. `_network_guard` uses `patch.object`, which IS
restore-safe under normal, strictly-LIFO pytest fixture finalization — proven by the probe
above and by the 684-test sweep. The leak my earlier mechanism-proof produced required
ARTIFICIAL out-of-order teardown of two overlapping windows, which does not occur in real
sequential pytest fixture teardown. The real defect was the monkeypatch *caller*, now fixed.
`_network_guard` retains only a LATENT fragility: it silently depends on every future layered
patch of `socket.socket.connect` also being LIFO-aware (i.e. `patch.object`, not
`monkeypatch.setattr`). That is a defense-in-depth consideration, not an active bug.

## caused_by / attribution
The transient monkeypatch version of `effect_spies` was introduced and fixed within the e9d5
change itself (Gerrit change 2436) — CI failed on the pre-fix patchset (runs 33333653370 /
33332386485 / 33331343082) and the landed commit d46c332c already carries the `patch.object`
fix + regression test. So the defect never landed on `main` in its broken form; edeb is the
tracking vehicle for a defect that was caught and corrected in-review under e9d5.
discovered_from = e9d5-c850-d505-4a5a (correct); caused_by = the same e9d5 work.

## Sibling failures (Step-7) — unchanged classification
test_atomic_completion_close.py, test_rebar_repo_isolation.py, test_tracker_footprint_cli.py
remain a SEPARATE git/filesystem resource-contention class; they share no code path with the
socket guard and are out of scope for this ticket.

## Disposition — escalating (no auto-apply, no auto-close)
Because the active root cause is ALREADY remediated on origin/main (fix + regression test
landed, and I verified the flake no longer reproduces), there is no new code change required
to resolve this flake. Per the debug protocol I am NOT auto-applying a speculative change and
NOT unilaterally closing. Two options for a human decision:
  (A) Close edeb as RESOLVED — root-caused (effect_spies monkeypatch collision), fixed in
      d46c332c under e9d5 with a landed regression test, verified no repro on current main.
      This satisfies the ticket's acceptance criteria (root cause identified + fix applied +
      test demonstrated stable).
  (B) Optional defense-in-depth follow-up (separate ticket or a small test-only change here):
      make `_network_guard` self-healing so a FUTURE monkeypatch-style caller cannot silently
      re-break the allow_network contract (e.g. clear any leaked local `connect` override on
      entry in the allow_network branch, and restore via unconditional delattr of our own
      override). Low-risk, test-only, but a design choice — not required to fix the flake.
Recommendation: (A) now; (B) only if the team wants belt-and-braces against re-introduction.
